## Preface

This is the data collection script for the SDM NN. I originally used the environmental data in AusAMF and two other datasets, but I don't think I have enough environmental information to calculate distributions.

So, we are starting from scratch here.

The assumed working directory is the jobs folder.

## Libraries
```{r}
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(tidyterra)
```
## Projection Paths
```{r}
#Rorqual does not have internet access on the node I need, so I saved the tif grid for conversion to CRS 3577
local_grid = file.path("/home/herna499/links/projects/def-jstinchc/herna499/proj_data")

Sys.setenv(PROJ_DATA = local_grid)
Sys.setenv(PROJ_LIB  = local_grid)
Sys.setenv(PROJ_NETWORK = "OFF")
Sys.setenv(GDAL_HTTP_MAX_RETRY = "0")

message("PROJ Search Paths: ", paste(sf_proj_search_paths(), collapse = ", "))

sf_proj_network(enable = FALSE)
```


## AusAMF
AusAMF datasets that are likely to overlap with other data sources are prefaced with `AA_`

```{r}
# load in abundance matrices, metadata, and taxonomy
abundance = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/abundance_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)
AA_metadata = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/sample_metadata.csv")
AA_filtering = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/filtering_info.csv")
AA_taxonomy = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/VT_taxonomy.csv")

# env_cube for environmental data from AusAMF
# input data for raster files is downloaded from the cited figshare in the manuscript
# https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28817378.v1
env_cube = rast("../raw_data/AusAMF/AusAMF_env_cube.tif")
env_cube = rename(env_cube, total_N = Total_N, avail_P = Avail_P, totalP = Total_P, elevation = Elevation, pH_cacl = pH) # this is just to keep names the same between the original metadata and that in the environmental cube. The mismatch is from the original paper.

# crop to match spatial extent of Australia
tocrop = terra::ext(112, 112+0.025*1681, -44, -44+0.025*1361)
env_cube = terra::crop(env_cube, tocrop)

# project data cube
AA_envcube = project(
  x = env_cube,
  y = "EPSG:3577",
  method = "bilinear",
  use_gdal = TRUE
)
```

## NVIS 7.0
This is the vegetation layer from NVIS V7.0. I will preface this data with `NV_`.
```{r}
# check available layers from `.gdb` file
gdb_path = "../raw_data/NVIS_V7/NVIS_V7_0_VECTOR_STATE_FILES_EXT.gdb/"
NV_avail_layers = st_layers(gdb_path)
NV_avail_layers$name

# create a list to store layers
# layers 1-8 are the vector layers. 9 and 10 are mapping tables to convert numerical IDs to vegetation types
NV_layers = lapply(NV_avail_layers$name[1:8], function(x) {
  vect(gdb_path, layer = x, proxy = TRUE)
  }
)

NV_details = as.data.frame(vect(gdb_path, layer = NV_avail_layers$name[9]))
NV_flat = as.data.frame(vect(gdb_path, layer = NV_avail_layers$name[10]))
```

## TERN
`TE_` prefixes. There is a lot of environmental raster data. So, let's combine into a raster data cube. Match extent of env_cube

```{r}
TE_files = list.files("../raw_data/tern/", full.names = TRUE)

# I confirmed the tern files are in the same crs as the env_cube the bounding box is based on.

# The maps are high resolution and large, so it's easy to crash the computer when cropping all layers at the same time. Here, we will do the cropping layer by layer in a loop.
TE_cube = vector("list", length(TE_files))

for (i in seq_along(TE_files)) {
  cat("Processing file", i, "of", length(TE_files), "\n")
  
  r = rast(TE_files[i])
  r_crop = terra::crop(r, tocrop)
  
  TE_cube[[i]] = r_crop
  
  # to save memory, we will remove the variables not in the data cube in the for loop
  rm(r, r_crop)
  gc()
}

# some of the grids are just slightly off in terms of extent, origin, and dimension. Like vvvvveeeeerrrrrryyyyy small differences. This creates an issue when trying to collapse them into a single data cube. The issue is in the quarterly NDVI measurements. We will resample those based on the TE_cube layer
template = rast(TE_files[1])
NDVI_files = TE_files[11:14]
NDVI_aligned = vector("list", length(NDVI_files))

for (i in seq_along(NDVI_files)) {
  cat("Processing NDVI layer", i, "\n")

  r = rast(NDVI_files[i])

  # Align to reference grid
  r_aligned = terra::resample(
    r,
    template,
    method = "bilinear"
  )

  # Crop to desired extent
  r_aligned = terra::crop(r_aligned, tocrop)

  NDVI_aligned[[i]] = r_aligned

  rm(r, r_aligned)
  gc()
}

# replace the misaligned NDVI files
TE_cube[11:14] = NDVI_aligned

# combine cropped layers into a data cube
TE_cube = rast(TE_cube)

# reproject TE_cube
TE_cube = project(
  x = TE_cube,
  y = "EPSG:3577",
  method = "bilinear",
  use_gdal = TRUE,
  filename = "../processed_data/TE_cube_projection.tif"
)
```

```{r}
# potential work around for R crashing. It shouldn't be a memory issue, but just in case, let's let terra use a temp directory and override the default terra limits by using BIGTIFF=YES.

# Set temporary directory
terra_tmp = "../processed_data/terra_temp"

dir.create(
  terra_tmp,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

terraOptions(
  tempdir = terra_tmp,
  memfrac = 0.5,
  progress = 1
)

# Combine layers
TE_cube = rast(TE_cube)

# Check the raster before projecting
print(TE_cube)

# Project to EPSG:3577
TE_cube = project(
  x = TE_cube,
  y = "EPSG:3577",
  method = "bilinear",
  use_gdal = TRUE,
  filename = "../processed_data/TE_cube_projection.tif",
  overwrite = TRUE,
  wopt = list(
    gdal = c("BIGTIFF=YES")
  )
)

```
